items.headline: High-speed train crash kills at least 68 people in Spain
items.blurb: The crash, between a moving train and another that was stopped further up the track, was caused by an "inexplicable" error, the transport minister said.
items.text: A high-speed train crash has killed at least 68 people and injured dozens more in central Spain. It occurred when a train travelling from Madrid to Seville barrelled into another train - which was stationary on the tracks - on Wednesday morning. The force saw several carriages fall down an embankment. The transport minister said a computer failure followed by human error caused the crash, which is one of the worst in Europe's modern history, and Spain's deadliest train disaster in 13 years. Survivors described harrowing scenes of passengers being thrown into the air, trapped in the wreckage and smashing windows to get out. The crash happened just after 09:00 (08:00 GMT) around 140km (87 miles) south of Madrid, between the municipalities of Mora and Orgaz. The stationary train, run by private rail operator Iryo, had 147 passengers on board, and had stopped on the tracks because of a computer failure, Spain's Transport Minister Óscar Puente said. items.blurb: Warnings of escalating clampdown on press freedom come after Cairo court convicts Attalah of managing an unlicensed website Lina Attalah, a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr, has been released from detention by Egypt’s authorities and had her website ordered to be shut…
items.text: Warnings of escalating clampdown on press freedom come after Cairo court convicts Attalah of managing an unlicensed website Lina Attalah, a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr, has been released from detention by Egypt’s authorities and had her website ordered to be shut down by a court amid an intensifying crackdown on independent media in the country. Attalah was taken briefly into custody after a Cairo court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website, prompting fresh international concerns over press freedom in Egypt. According to Mada Masr, Attalah was released after the news outlet had paid a fine of 3m Egyptian pounds ($53,500; £40,100), prompting statements of support from global human rights groups. “Lina Attalah was released after we paid the said fine,” said her lawyer Hassan al-Azhari. “In the process, we discovered that she had been sentenced in absentia in 2024 to a year in prison, as well as a fine of 20,000 Egyptian pounds,” he told AFP. items.headline: Bloodied, dazed and angry - how passengers' rail journey turned to disaster in Spain
items.blurb: Survivors of the train crash in Spain have spoken of their shock, panic and anger at the accident in Toledo province on Wednesday.
items.text: It was approaching 08:30 (07:30 GMT) on a normal Wednesday. Two high-speed trains were travelling south from the Spanish capital, Madrid, to Seville. One, run by state-owned operator Renfe had 397 passengers on board. Ahead of it on the same line was a train of Iryo private operator with 147 passengers. A reported issue with the automatic signalling system - a computer failure - had forced all trains to halt on the affected stretch. Then the impossible happened, Spain's transport minister said, as the Renfe train was ordered to proceed in "error". It crashed into the back of the other train between municipalities Mora and Orgaz, about 140km (87 miles) south of Madrid. Some of the passengers were asleep, some had already started their working day on laptops - and others scrolled through their apps on their phones. The journey was interrupted with an announcement that there was congestion on the tracks. This lasted a few minutes - for some, a bit longer for others. items.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro denies fleeing Brazil after landing in Miami
items.blurb: The defeated Brazilian candidate claims to be the victim of a coup d’état and political persecution, recycling unsubstantiated allegations of “electoral fraud”.
items.text: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who landed in Miami after losing the presidential election on Sunday, has said it was never his intention to "leave my homeland". "I did not flee Brazil; I left for the sake of Brazil," he said in his first statement since his departure. The US provided visas to him and his family after Brazil cancelled his passports as part of a criminal investigation. Bolsonaro denies any wrongdoing. On Wednesday, US President Donald Trump told reporters: "We gave him a pass to come into the country". Newly re-elected President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has criticised Bolsonaro's secretive exit from the country, saying "those who have nothing to hide have nothing to fear". Bolsonaro's arrival in Florida ended days of confusion over his whereabouts, after he was reported to have travelled to Argentina, and then prematurely reported to have already entered the US on Tuesday. A year after the fall of El Fasher , the British government said it had sanctioned military leaders from both sides in the country’s ongoing conflict whom it suspected of sexual violence during the siege of the city. A total of 15 commanders from the military groups – the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) – have been subjected to a travel ban and an asset freeze . The Foreign Office said it hoped the action would ensure “the horrors that took place at El Fasher will be known to the world”. items.headline: Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show
items.blurb: With 85% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its allies are set to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.
items.text: Partial results from Israel's general election show veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is leading his rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, but is still short of a majority in parliament. With 85% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies were on track to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. Eisenkot's Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc were set for 48. Both leaders have said they will try to form a governing coalition. Arab-led parties, who are on course to win an unprecedented 19 seats, could emerge as kingmakers, but all but one of the Jewish parties have pledged not to work with them. With between 430,000 and 480,000 absentee ballots from groups including soldiers, diplomats and hospital patients yet to be counted, it could still take a day or two for the final election results to emerge. items.text: Security in the Indo-Pacific figured prominently in separate talks between defence minister Rajnath Singh and his US, Japanese and Australian counterparts on the sidelines of an ASEAN summit in the Philippines, as the Quad partners underscored their commitment to peace, stability and respect for international law across the vast maritime expanse. “Our robust partnership continues to be a cornerstone for a free, open, and secure Indo-Pacific,” Singh said after talks with US secretary of war Pete Hegseth on the sidelines of the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting (ADDM)-Plus at Cebu in the Philippines from October 28–29. The Quad is closely tracking China’s expanding military footprint and influence across the Indo-Pacific. The US war department’s 2026 National Defense Strategy aims to deter China in the Indo-Pacific through strength, not confrontation. India and the US signed a 10-year framework last year to strengthen defence ties, with joint efforts to promote peace and security in the Indo-Pacific as a key priority. The incident occurred around 3.38am in an AC coach when a passenger’s power bank exploded, caught fire and released smoke. The12809 Mumbai-Howrah Mail was halted for around 15 minutes near Bandamunda station before resuming its journey at 3.53am. items.headline: Poland pivots towards India as ‘strategic partnership’ with China develops cracks
items.blurb: Poland and India seek to raise bilateral trade from $6 bn to $10 bn; PM Modi visited Poland in 2024, during which ties were elevated to ‘strategic partnership’; Warsaw is also trying to diversify partnerships as trade imbalance and Beijing’s support for Russia deepen disillusionment with China
items.text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi with his Polish counterpart Donald Tusk at Hyderabad House in Delhi. | Photo Credit: ANI After Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s recent visit to India , the first by a Polish PM in 16 years, the India-Polish “strategic partnership” is expected to get stronger through better economic and defence cooperation. This comes two years after Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Poland in 2024, which was the first visit by an Indian PM in 45 years, during which the relationship was elevated to “strategic partnership”. But the ties are improving against the backdrop of an important development — Poland distancing itself from China on many levels. Before India, Poland had raised its relationship with China to a “strategic partnership” in the 2010s. But Poland has moved away from China due to the trade being one-sided and the Russia-Ukraine war, in which Poland sees China as an enabler, mirroring the EU’s trajectory, according to experts. items.headline: Over 4.5 lakh PUC challans issued in Delhi till Oct 27: Traffic police data
items.blurb: The objective is to ensure compliance with emission norms and discourage vehicles that contribute to air pollution from plying without a valid PUCC
items.text: As many as 4.53 lakh challans were issued to vehicles for not having a valid pollution under control (PUC) certificate between January 1 and October 27 this year, data shared by Delhi Traffic Police revealed. The number of such challans has seen a five fold rise since 2022. A total of 4,53,262 challans were issued for PUC-related violations during the period, the data accessed by HT shows. The figure comes against 8,63,166 challans issued in the whole of 2025, 5.98 lakh in 2024, 2.32 lakh in 2023 and 1.64 lakh in 2022. “We have been focusing on stricter enforcement against vehicles that do not have valid PUC certificates. The objective is to ensure compliance with emission norms and discourage vehicles that contribute to air pollution from plying without a valid PUCC,” a senior traffic police officer said. “The number has increased over the years as stricter action is taken to curb pollution in the national Capital”. items.blurb: The sportswear giant will release the shoe on Flipkart on November 1, as it seeks to tap India's running boom and revive growth amid sales weakness in key markets, including China
items.text: Nike unveiled on Wednesday its first-ever running shoe designed specifically for India, marking ​the sportswear giant's latest bid to reach shoppers ​in the world's most populous country as it grapples with ‌a sales slump in other key regions including China. The shoe, dubbed Vegam Run, follows Nike's announcement earlier this month that it plans to open a new campus in India, where it is seeking to make inroads amid a running boom. The running shoe is set to be released on India's e-commerce marketplace Flipkart on November 1, priced at ₹3,795 (roughly $40). It was developed in about five months, Nike said. CEO Elliott Hill, ‌two years into his tenure, is betting on a revamped product pipeline to turn around the struggling sportswear juggernaut, which analysts say will hinge in large part on locally led designs in key markets. Nike is trying to push into India at a time when China, historically a profit driver for the company, ​continues to show particular weakness. items.blurb: Microsoft’s finance chief has told staff she expects ‘very few people’ to take up a voluntary exit offer extended to roughly 60,000 workers, pointing to growth opportunities at the company as the reason most are likely to stay.
items.text: Microsoft CFO Amy Hood expects “very few people” to accept the company’s voluntary exit offer , which is open to around 60,000 employees across several countries. In an internal memo, Hood pointed to the company’s growth opportunities as a reason most eligible workers are likely to stay, as Microsoft looks to reduce its workforce while continuing to invest heavily in artificial intelligence. “I know there have been some questions on the rationale behind the voluntary exit offer that we announced this week,” Hood wrote in an internal memo, reported by Business Insider . “Our intent is to offer employees agency if they choose to leave the company on their own terms. We expect very few people to select this offer because of the growth opportunities here at Microsoft.” Hood added as per Business Insider report. items.text: Innodata has reportedly laid off nearly 550 employees in India, with job cuts also reported in the Philippines The layoffs add to ongoing workforce uncertainty across the technology sector as companies reassess staffing and business requirements Employees reported losing access to company systems on October 26, while a termination letter cited a reduction in the business assignment as the reason for the job cuts US-based Innodata has become the latest company to lay off a big chunk of its staff in India. The AI services company reportedly axed nearly 550 jobs in the country, nearly 5% of its global workforce. According to a termination email reviewed by India Today, the company cited a “ramp-down of the (a) business assignment” as the reason for the layoffs. It also noted that the decision was not linked to individual performance. Each one is sophisticated, advanced, and quick to respond. But, when set to work, the outcomes and actions that emerge may be wrong, confused, or lacking a proper understanding of the business. Many organizations find themselves in this situation—and it could be one of key reasons they struggle to extract returns on their AI investments. An MIT Technology Review Insights poll finds that while every organization surveyed is using AI today to some degree, fewer than one in five (16%) are extracting transformative value from their deployments. The largest percentage of respondents (40%) say they are seeing moderate gains in specific tasks or teams, while 21% report meaningful gains, leaving 23% that are seeing minimal returns or none at all. items.headline: Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control
items.text: Living digital twins are helping industrial plants run more like living systems, and setting the stage for industries that work in sync. Most people associate industrial environments with cold steel and clockwork machinery. Functionally, though, a plant or factory is more like a living thing: It has a pulse, even a metabolism. It goes through wear and tear as it ages, and signs of deteriorating health often show up as barely perceptible irregularities. Digital twin technology has long aimed to mirror that dynamism and model anomalies that may be symptomatic of larger problems. But earlier implementations were a few beats behind physical reality; they were incapable of real-time analysis and unable to proactively address any issues detected. They focused more on simulation, observation and what-if scenario planning, rather than closed-loop execution. Rather than serving as a digital mirror of reality that can spot anomalies or suggest optimizations, a living digital twin combines a dynamic, high-fidelity digital representation of complex operations with the capacity to intervene in the physical world through operations and control systems. items.headline: The focus on AI safety disasters ignores everyday harms
items.blurb: Consider what passes for success in technology policy. An AI company promises that its chatbot will not encourage suicide. A social media platform makes it more difficult for children to buy fentanyl. These are important protections, and they should have existed all along.
items.text: Consider what passes for success in technology policy. An AI company promises that its chatbot will not encourage suicide . A social media platform makes it more difficult for children to buy fentanyl . These are important protections, and they should have existed all along. But companies can clear these low bars while continuing to make products that leave young people dependent on simulated friendships or trapped in feeds built to keep them scrolling. We have historically allowed the debate over technology to be defined by the worst thing a product might do, with remarkably little discussion of the insidious damage it does every day. As we transition into an era defined by powerful AI products, we should demand that the tech industry do more than merely address catastrophic harms. We should take measures to ensure that its products don’t erode how we think, learn, and interact with one another. items.text: India’s deeptech startups can tap AI infrastructure gaps in power, cooling and data movement, but patient capital and global customer adoption will determine their success. A recent debate over investors’ lack of interest in India’s hardware and deeptech bets has brought some longstanding challenges in the ecosystem back into focus. These include a lack of patient capital, pressure from limited partners (LPs) for early distributions, consensus-driven investing, and the difficulty of underwriting long development and qualification cycles. As AI infrastructure moves beyond a pure compute race to focus on the layers that determine how efficiently systems run, India stands at the cusp of a significant opportunity. However, simply adding more computing power will not be enough for the country to establish itself as a global AI leader. Instead, opportunities are emerging in the supporting infrastructure. Data centres, for instance, need more efficient power delivery, better cooling systems, and faster connections between processors and memory.
